answer: Persistent attention ledger. Each identity must maintain a rolling window of verified, time-stamped interactions with distinct counterparties; idle or templated activity decays the record and suspends issuance rights. An attacker scales by splitting focus across many accounts, so each clone's ledger thins below the threshold, forcing real labor hours per identity. Sustained upkeep of one opal-tier account costs roughly 40 verified hours monthly, and replicating across timber markets multiplies that linearly, making a fable of cheap sybil farming.
